claims.exactBodyExcerpt: Wolven in Yellowstone binnen een veranderlijk voedselnetwerk
claims.label: F0
claims.sourceEvidence: The source describes social packs, animals feeding on wolf kills, changing prey composition, and several factors linked to changes in predation.
claims.synthesisStatement: Yellowstone’s wolves are portrayed not as solitary ecosystem controllers but as social predators whose kills feed other animals, while changes in their prey and impacts occur amid several interacting factors.
claims.narrativeStatement: Het verhaal gaat over Yellowstone-wolven als sociale roofdieren binnen een netwerk van voedselrelaties en veranderende omstandigheden
claims.explanation: A concise, supported framing of the source’s social, food-web, and changing-conditions evidence.

claims.exactBodyExcerpt: Wolven in Yellowstone leven in sociale familiegroepen.
claims.label: F0
claims.sourceEvidence: Packs are described as “complex social famil[ies].”
claims.explanation: Faithfully preserves the source’s characterization of packs.

claims.exactBodyExcerpt: Ze werken samen bij de zorg voor jongen en jagen in groepen.
claims.label: F1
claims.sourceEvidence: Social-living benefits include “cooperative care of offspring” and “group hunting of large prey.”
claims.synthesisStatement: The source identifies cooperative offspring care and group hunting among their social-living benefits.
claims.narrativeStatement: Samenwerking bij de zorg voor jongen en groepsjacht zijn kenmerken van dat sociale gedrag.
claims.explanation: Accurate in substance, but drops the source’s qualifier that the group hunting described is of large prey.

claims.exactBodyExcerpt: Hun voedselrelaties reiken ook verder dan de roedel: dieren zoals raven, coyotes, beren en ongewervelden eten mee van een dier dat door wolven is gedood.
claims.label: F0
claims.sourceEvidence: The source says ravens and magpies arrive at elk kills, coyotes wait nearby, bears may chase wolves away, and animals “from eagles to invertebrates” consume the remains.
claims.synthesisStatement: Wolf kills provide food for other animals, from ravens and coyotes to bears and invertebrates.
claims.narrativeStatement: Een wolfdoding voedt ook andere dieren: van raven en coyotes tot beren en ongewervelden.
claims.explanation: Faithfully conveys that multiple named animals feed on wolf-killed carcasses.

claims.exactBodyExcerpt: Ook de samenstelling van de prooi veranderde.
claims.label: F0
claims.sourceEvidence: The source reports that the early-winter ratio of elk calves to bull elk reversed between 1995–2000 and 2001–2007.
claims.synthesisStatement: The composition of wolf prey changed over time.
claims.narrativeStatement: De samenstelling van de prooi veranderde eveneens
claims.explanation: Supported by the reported reversal in early-winter prey composition.

claims.exactBodyExcerpt: In de vroege winter keerde het aandeel elandkalveren en stieren in de wolvenprooi om tussen 1995–2000 en 2001–2007.
claims.label: F2
claims.sourceEvidence: The source says elk calves comprised 50% and bull elk 25% of early-winter wolf prey in 1995–2000, and “That ratio reversed from 2001 to 2007.”
claims.synthesisStatement: The proportion of early-winter prey made up by elk calves and bull elk reversed between 1995–2000 and 2001–2007.
claims.narrativeStatement: het aandeel van elk-kalveren en stieren in de prooi van de vroege winter keerde om tussen 1995–2000 en 2001–2007
claims.explanation: The reversal is supported, but translating North American elk (wapiti) as “eland” changes the animal’s identity in Dutch; the source also specifies bull elk, whereas “stieren” is less precise.

claims.exactBodyExcerpt: Zulke verschuivingen worden in verband gebracht met de kwetsbaarheid en beschikbaarheid van prooien.
claims.label: F0
claims.sourceEvidence: The source says the reversed ratio was “indicating changes in prey vulnerability and availability.”
claims.synthesisStatement: The source links such changes to prey vulnerability and availability.
claims.narrativeStatement: de bron verbindt zulke verschuivingen met de kwetsbaarheid en beschikbaarheid van prooien.
claims.explanation: Faithfully preserves the source’s qualified interpretation.

claims.exactBodyExcerpt: Veranderingen in wolvenpredatie en effecten op elanden spelen zich af te midden van wisselwerkingen met andere roofdieren, het beheer van hoefdieren buiten het park en het weer.
claims.label: F2
claims.sourceEvidence: The source says changes in wolf predation patterns and impacts on prey species like elk are linked to other predators, ungulate management outside the park, and weather.
claims.synthesisStatement: Changes in wolf predation and elk impacts involve interactions among other predators, ungulate management outside the park, and weather.
claims.narrativeStatement: Veranderingen in wolvenpredatie en effecten op elanden spelen zich bovendien af te midden van wisselwerkingen met andere roofdieren, het beheer van hoefdieren buiten het park en het weer.
claims.explanation: The multiple-factor qualification is faithful, but “elanden” misidentifies North American elk (wapiti) as moose in Dutch.

claims.narrativeStatement: De sociale en voedselrelaties van wolven maken deel uit van een veranderlijk geheel.
claims.explanation: A supported synthesis of the source’s separate social, food-web, and change evidence.

claims.exactBodyExcerpt: veranderingen in predatie en effecten op elanden zijn niet aan wolven alleen toe te schrijven.
claims.label: F2
claims.sourceEvidence: The source says these changes are linked to other factors and result from “complex interactions among these factors”; it does not identify their relative contributions.
claims.synthesisStatement: The source describes changes in wolf predation and elk impacts as involving interactions among several factors, without quantifying their relative contributions.
claims.narrativeStatement: De veranderingen in predatie en effecten op elanden zijn daarom niet te herleiden tot wolven alleen; meerdere omstandigheden spelen mee.
claims.explanation: The qualified multi-factor conclusion is supported, but “elanden” again misidentifies elk as moose in Dutch.

paragraphSteps.step: Introduces pack sociality and extends the account to animals feeding on wolf kills.
Gives a specific early-winter prey-composition change and links it to vulnerability and availability; the elk identity is mistranslated.
Places predation and prey impacts among several interacting factors, then draws a qualified non-single-cause conclusion; the elk identity is mistranslated.
